subject: social_science

concepts.title: Street Vending and Self-Employment
concepts.definition: Individuals who manage their own small-scale trade or services on city roadsides using temporary setups, carts, or pavement space.
concepts.key_idea: Self-managed work with no employer and temporary physical structures.
question_patterns: Describe the nature of work for street vendors
How do street workers organize their own business?
What kind of shops do people set up on the pavement?
Why do street vendors have no job security?
What percentage of city workers are street vendors in some surveys?

solution_steps.explain: Street vendors are self-employed and do not have an employer.
Shops are often temporary, such as boards on boxes or canvas sheets.

concepts.title: Calculating Net Daily Savings
concepts.definition: The amount of money remaining with a worker after deducting daily living costs like food and rent from their total daily earnings.
concepts.key_idea: The surplus income available to a worker for family support or future use.
question_patterns: How much does a worker save if they earn {daily_earnings} and spend {daily_expenses}?
Calculate the daily savings of a rickshaw puller earning {daily_earnings} with costs of {daily_expenses}
What is the net amount left for the family if daily income is {daily_earnings} and expenses are {daily_expenses}?
Find the remaining money after a worker spends {daily_expenses} out of {daily_earnings}
Determine the daily surplus for a worker earning {daily_earnings} and paying {daily_expenses} for rent and food

solution_steps.explain: The net savings is the difference between total daily income and total daily costs.

concepts.title: Legal Recognition of Hawkers
concepts.definition: The policy shift recognizing street vending as a legitimate right to livelihood rather than just a traffic obstruction.
concepts.key_idea: Balancing the right to earn a living with the need for smooth traffic flow through hawking zones.
question_patterns: What are hawking zones?
How has the government's view on street vending changed?
What rights do street vendors have according to new suggestions?
Why should hawkers be part of decision-making committees?
What was street vending previously considered by authorities?

solution_steps.explain: Vending is now recognized as a general benefit and a right to earn a livelihood.

concepts.title: Permanent Market Shops
concepts.definition: Established retail businesses in designated market areas that hold municipal licenses and often hire supervisors and helpers.
concepts.key_idea: Regulated commerce in fixed locations with formal licensing and staff management.
question_patterns: How do permanent shops in the market differ from street stalls?
What is the role of the Municipal Corporation in city markets?
What do businesspersons like Harpreet and Vandana do to run their showroom?
Who gives the license to permanent shops to do business?
Why do permanent shops employ supervisors and helpers?

solution_steps.explain: Permanent shops must be given a license by the municipal corporation.

concepts.title: Labour Chowk and Daily Wage Work
concepts.definition: A specific location in a city where daily wage labourers gather to be hired by contractors for manual tasks.
concepts.key_idea: Informal assembly point for casual workers seeking manual labor opportunities.
question_patterns: What is a labour chowk?
What kind of work do people at the labour chowk do?
Who are daily wage labourers?
Where do casual workers wait for work in the city?
List the tasks performed by workers hired at a labour chowk

solution_steps.explain: Labour chowk is a crossing where workers wait with tools for employers.

concepts.title: Casual Employment and Job Insecurity
concepts.definition: A work arrangement where employees are hired on a temporary basis, usually during peak seasons, without long-term contracts or benefits.
concepts.key_idea: Employment that lacks stability and depends entirely on the employer's immediate needs.
question_patterns: What does it mean to be employed on a casual basis?
Why is there no job security for workers like Nirmala?
When are casual workers usually asked to leave?
Describe the working conditions in casual factory units
What happens to casual workers when the work season ends?

solution_steps.explain: Workers are required to come only as and when the employer needs them.

concepts.title: Total Daily Factory Wages
concepts.definition: The total compensation a factory worker receives for a day, including their base pay for standard hours and extra pay for overtime.
concepts.key_idea: Summing regular pay and additional incentives for extra work hours.
question_patterns: Calculate the total daily pay if standard rate is {standard_rate} and overtime is {overtime_rate}
What is the total wage for a worker earning {standard_rate} base and {overtime_rate} extra?
Find the daily income of a tailor with {standard_rate} pay and {overtime_rate} for late work
How much does Nirmala earn in a day if she gets {standard_rate} for 8 hours and {overtime_rate} for extra hours?
Determine the total daily earnings given a base of {standard_rate} and overtime of {overtime_rate}

solution_steps.explain: The total daily wage is the sum of the standard daily rate and the overtime payment.

concepts.title: Regular and Permanent Employment
concepts.definition: Stable jobs in offices or government departments where workers receive a regular monthly salary and have long-term job security.
concepts.key_idea: Consistent employment with a fixed workplace and predictable income.
question_patterns: What are the features of a permanent job?
How is a regular worker different from a casual worker?
Why do permanent workers have more security?
What kind of work does a marketing manager like Sudha do?
Describe the benefits of being a regular employee

solution_steps.explain: Permanent workers can expect their job to continue for a long period.

concepts.title: Social Security and Employee Benefits
concepts.definition: Additional financial and health protections provided to permanent workers, such as provident funds, medical insurance, and paid leave.
concepts.key_idea: Non-wage compensation that supports a worker's health and retirement.
question_patterns: What benefits does Sudha get along with her salary?
Explain the concept of savings for old age in permanent jobs
What is medical leave in the context of regular employment?
How do holidays work for permanent office employees?
What happens to the part of the salary kept with the government?

solution_steps.explain: Benefits include old age savings (PF), holidays, and medical facilities.

concepts.title: Call Centres in Big Cities
concepts.definition: Centralized offices equipped with computers and telephones to handle consumer queries and services for domestic or foreign companies.
concepts.key_idea: A modern form of urban employment providing services via telecommunication.
question_patterns: What is a call centre?
Why do foreign companies set up call centres in India?
What kind of services do call centres provide?
Describe the setup of a typical call centre workstation
Why is call centre work considered a new form of employment?

solution_steps.explain: Call centres deal with problems and questions regarding goods and services.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Bachchu Manjhi earns {daily_earnings} every day and spends {daily_expenses} on his food and rent. How much does he save daily?

Nirmala is paid {standard_rate} for a normal day and {overtime_rate} extra for working late. What is her total daily wage?

solution_template.explain: Total Wage = Standard Rate + Overtime Rate

worked_examples.question_pattern: A factory worker receives a base pay of {standard_rate} and an additional {overtime_rate} for urgent work. Find the total earnings for that day.

solution_template.explain: Total Wage = Standard Rate + Overtime Rate
